title: RoboCasa House Simulator
summary: A RoboCasa-backed, single-storey apartment-style house with a closed floor plan, connected rooms, and an articulated SO-101 arm mounted on a kitchen table, launched through one generic script in headless or interactive mode.

environments.scene: A closed single-storey apartment with an outer wall perimeter, interior partition walls, traversable doorway gaps, a kitchen, and a kitchen table supporting the SO-101 arm.

runtimes.description: The generic launcher validates its arguments, activates simulator/.venv, and starts the RoboCasa-backed house with a viewer by default or without one when --headless is supplied.

constraints.description: The project is managed with uv and uses the virtual environment at simulator/.venv.
The installed and imported simulation framework is RoboCasa, using its MuJoCo and robosuite runtime dependencies.
The world is a closed, single-storey apartment-style floor plan with a collidable floor, complete outer perimeter, interior partition walls, and doorway gaps wide enough to traverse.
The simulated robot is an articulated SO-101 arm described in URDF and mounted securely on a table in the kitchen.
A single executable run_env.sh requires --env <runtime>, supports --headless and --no-headless, defaults to an interactive viewer, launches robocasa, and rejects unsupported or conflicting arguments.

Automated checks validate the documents, compile the scene, verify the floor plan and robot structure, and exercise the launcher headlessly without downloading the optional multi-gigabyte RoboCasa kitchen asset bundle.
